method.text: Each point is the centre of a 21 x 21 grid of elevation samples spaced 500 m apart (a 10 km x 10 km box). At the centre, rows run north and columns run east. Every sample is placed with the spherical destination-point formula (distance sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2), bearing atan2(dx, dy) from the centre) on a sphere with the body's mean radius (Earth 6,371,008.8 m; Moon 1,737,400 m; Mars 3,389,500 m), so the grid stays valid near the poles. At each of the 19 x 19 = 361 interior samples, dz/dx and dz/dy are central differences over the 1 km (2 x 500 m) baseline, and slope = atan(sqrt((dz/dx)^2 + (dz/dy)^2)) in degrees. Statistics: median, mean and 90th percentile of the 361 slopes (percentile by linear interpolation, Python statistics.quantiles 'inclusive'); percent of slope cells below 8, below 10 and below 15 degrees (pct_lt_8, pct_lt_10, pct_lt_15); max_flat_square_km = side of the largest square of interior samples in which every slope is below 10 degrees (NASA's Artemis III landing slope limit), in 500 m steps from 0.5 to 9.5 km (0 if no sample qualifies), which the landing-zone pillar uses; relief = highest minus lowest of the 441 elevations; elevation of the centre sample; flat_water_suspect = true when at least 20% of the samples share one identical elevation (lakes or sea surfaces, which the Copernicus DEM flattens; also salt flats). Slopes at a 1 km baseline describe kilometre-scale terrain, not boulders or metre-scale roughness, and depend on each DEM's resolution (about 90 m Earth, 237 m Moon, 463 m Mars), so comparisons across bodies are approximate.

datasets.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-90 (2021 release) via the Open-Meteo Elevation API
datasets.resolution: 3 arc-seconds (~90 m; longitude spacing widens above 50 deg latitude). The API returns the value of the DEM pixel that contains each coordinate (no interpolation).
datasets.elev_datum: m above the EGM2008 geoid (Copernicus DEM; horizontal datum WGS84-G1150)
datasets.licence: Copernicus DEM GLO-90 is free to use under the Copernicus DEM licence (ESA). Open-Meteo API data: CC BY 4.0; the free API is for non-commercial use (600 calls/min, 5,000/h, 10,000/day; each coordinate counts as one call).
datasets.credit: Produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-90 (c) DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and (c) Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved. Elevation API by Open-Meteo.com.
datasets.caveats: Copernicus DEM flattens lakes and seas to a single height, which is what the flat_water_suspect flag detects. Values come back in whole metres.

datasets.name: LRO LOLA DEM Global 128 ppd v04 (NASA Solar System Treks, Moon Trek)
datasets.resolution: 128 pixels per degree (~237 m at the equator), float32. Sampled with ArcGIS getSamples, bilinear interpolation.
datasets.elev_datum: m relative to the 1,737,400 m reference sphere (Moon 2000; radius = value + 1,737,400 m)
datasets.coordinates: GCS_Moon_2000 (wkid 104903): latitude, longitude east-positive -180..180; service extent -180..180 / -90..90
datasets.licence: NASA data; Trek metadata: 'Access constraints: None; Use constraints: None'.
datasets.credit: LOLA Instrument Team, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter); served by NASA Solar System Treks (trek.nasa.gov).
datasets.caveats: Pixels without LOLA shots are filled by interpolation; LOLA cross-track spacing is ~1.2 km at the equator and ~25 m above 85 deg, so near-equator slopes at a 1 km baseline are smoothed. Trek also serves higher-resolution LOLA DEMs that are NOT used here, to keep all Moon points consistent: LRO_LOLA_DEM_Global_256ppd_v06 (~118 m), LRO_LOLA_DEM_SPole75_30mp_v04 (30 m, polar stereographic, 75 S to the pole), LRO_LOLA_DEM_SPole875_5mp_v04 (5 m, 87.5 S to the pole).

datasets.name: MGS MOLA Global DEM, 128/64 ppd merge (NASA Solar System Treks, Mars Trek)
datasets.resolution: Blend of the 128 and 64 pixels-per-degree MOLA grids; most of the surface is at 128 ppd (~463 m at the equator), whose data are sparse above 87 N/S. 16-bit integer metres. Sampled with ArcGIS getSamples, bilinear interpolation.
datasets.elev_datum: m above the MOLA areoid (Mars geoid from gravity model GMM-2B, degree and order 50)
datasets.coordinates: GCS_Mars_2000 (wkid 104905): planetocentric latitude, longitude east-positive -180..180 (0..360 longitudes are not accepted by the service)
datasets.licence: NASA data, public domain (USGS Astrogeology lists the MOLA 463 m DEM as CC0).
datasets.credit: MOLA Science Team, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (Mars Global Surveyor); served by NASA Solar System Treks (trek.nasa.gov).
datasets.caveats: Gaps of 1-2 km between MOLA tracks are common (up to 12 km near the equator) and are interpolated, so slopes at a 1 km baseline are smoothed.
